content: 1. Administer cefepime intravenously (IV) or intramuscularly (IM) at a dose of 1 to 2 grams every 12 hours for 7 to 10 days for the treatment of severe urinary tract infections (UTIs) caused by Escherichia coli or Klebsiella pneumoniae. For severe cases, use 2 grams IV every 12 hours for 10 days. 2. For uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections, administer cefepime at a dose of 2 grams IV every 12 hours for 10 days. 3. For complicated intra-abdominal infections, administer cefepime at a dose of 2 grams IV every 12 hours for 7 to 10 days in combination with metronidazole. 4. Adjust the maintenance dosage of cefepime based on the patient’s creatinine clearance (CrCl). 5. For febrile neutropenic patients older than 2 months and weighing less than 40 kg, administer cefepime at a dose of 50 mg/kg IV every 8 hours for 7 days or until neutropenia resolves. Do not exceed 2 grams every 8 hours. 6. For moderate-to-severe pneumonia, administer cefepime at a dose of 50 mg/kg IV every 12 hours for 10 days. Do not exceed 2 grams every 12 hours. 7. For uncomplicated and complicated UTIs, including pyelonephritis, administer cefepime at a dose of 50 mg/kg IV or IM every 12 hours for 7 to 10 days. Do not exceed 2 grams every 12 hours. 8. Cefepime reduces the efficacy of the BCG intravesical live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Wait until antibiotic treatment is completed before administering live bacterial vaccines. 9. Cefepime reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 10. Cefepime reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Complete antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 11. Cefepime reduces the efficacy of live typhoid vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Wait until antibiotic treatment is completed before administering live bacterial vaccines. 12. Cefepime increases the toxicity of aminoglycosides such as amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, neomycin, plazomicin, streptomycin, and tobramycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor renal function closely when co-administering these agents. 13. Cefepime may increase the nephrotoxic effects of potent diuretics like furosemide. Monitor renal function closely if co-administered. Reports of nephrotoxicity with this combination are inconsistent. 14. Cefepime reduces the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors such as atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, cosibelimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, and toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of these agents. 15. Cefepime reduces the levels or effects of oral hormonal contraceptives such as ethinyl estradiol, dienogest/estradiol valerate, and levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution is advised. Consider using an alternative or additional form of birth control during concomitant use. 16. Cefepime increases the effects of warfarin by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as cefepime may decrease prothrombin activity. 17. Probenecid increases the levels or effects of cefepime by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Cefepime reduces the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering antibiotics with this combination.
